subject: Physics
prompt: Mean free path depends on temperature as (at const P)
explain: At constant P, n∝1/T, so λ=1/(√2πd²n) ∝ T.

subject: Physics
prompt: Number of collisions per second by a molecule (collision frequency)
explain: Collision frequency Z = √2 πd²n v_avg; λ = v_avg/Z.

subject: Physics
prompt: Ideal gas assumption about intermolecular forces
explain: In ideal gas model, intermolecular forces are assumed negligible.

subject: Physics
prompt: Degrees of freedom for linear triatomic molecule (room temp)
explain: Linear triatomic: 3 translational + 2 rotational + 2 vibrational = 7 DOF.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which quantity is same for all ideal gases at same T and P?
explain: By ideal gas law, PV=NkT → N/V = P/kT, same for all gases at same T,P.

subject: Physics
prompt: Degrees of freedom for a rigid diatomic molecule at high temp (vibrational active)?
explain: At high T: 3 translational + 2 rotational + 2 vibrational = 7 DOF.

subject: Physics
prompt: Boltzmann constant k has SI unit?
explain: k = R/Nₐ has unit J/K (joule per kelvin) per molecule.

subject: Physics
prompt: At same T, which gas has higher average kinetic energy per molecule?
explain: Translational KE = (3/2)kT for ALL gases regardless of type at same T.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which assumption of kinetic theory is about molecular collisions?
explain: Kinetic theory assumes all molecular collisions are perfectly elastic.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which law states that at same T and P, equal volumes contain equal molecules?
explain: Avogadro's law: equal volumes of gases at same T and P have equal number of molecules.

subject: Physics
prompt: At constant temperature, as pressure doubles, number density n of gas?
explain: n = P/kT; at constant T, n ∝ P, so doubling P doubles n.

subject: Physics
prompt: Cᵥ for diatomic gas at high temperature (f=7) per mole?
explain: At high T, vibrational modes activate; f=7 so Cᵥ = (7/2)R.

subject: Physics
prompt: Cₚ for diatomic gas at high temperature (f=7) per mole?
explain: Cₚ = (7/2)R + R = (9/2)R for diatomic at high temperature.

subject: Physics
prompt: At constant P, mean free path λ varies with T as?
explain: At const P, n ∝ 1/T, so λ = 1/(√2 πnd²) ∝ T.

subject: Physics
prompt: At constant T, mean free path λ varies with n (number density) as?
explain: λ = 1/(√2 πnd²); at constant T, λ inversely proportional to n.

subject: Physics
prompt: Collision frequency Z of a molecule varies with temperature as (const V)?
explain: Z = √2 πd²n v̄; at const V, n is const and v̄ ∝ √T, so Z ∝ √T.

subject: Physics
prompt: At same temperature, which quantity is larger: v̄ or vₘₚ?
explain: v̄ = √(8RT/πM) and vₘₚ = √(2RT/M); numerically v̄ > vₘₚ.

subject: Physics
prompt: The assumption that molecular size is negligible compared to separation means?
explain: Ideal gas treats molecules as point masses; volume of molecules ≪ container volume.

subject: Physics
prompt: At same T and V, heavier gas molecules hit the wall _____ than lighter ones.
explain: Heavier molecules have lower average speed at same T, so they collide with walls less frequently.

subject: Physics
prompt: Collision frequency Z of molecules varies with T at constant pressure as?
explain: At const P, n∝1/T and v̄∝√T; Z=√2·πd²·n·v̄ ∝ (1/T)·√T = 1/√T.

subject: Physics
prompt: As temperature increases, the Maxwell distribution curve height (peak value) ____.
explain: At higher T, molecules spread over wider speed range; peak shifts right and peak height decreases.

subject: Physics
prompt: Ratio of rms speed to mean free path at constant T: if d doubles, λ changes by?
explain: λ ∝ 1/d²; doubling d makes λ → λ/4.

subject: Physics
prompt: The pressure of an ideal gas is zero if the ______ is zero.
explain: P = nkT; at T=0, molecular KE and hence pressure vanish for an ideal gas.

subject: Physics
prompt: For an ideal gas mixture, internal energy U_total =?
explain: Internal energy is extensive; total U of mixture = sum of internal energies of each component.

subject: Physics
prompt: The mean free path of gas molecules is independent of?
explain: λ=1/(√2πd²n) depends on n and d only, not on mass or temperature (at constant n).

subject: Physics
prompt: For ideal gas, which quantity is independent of the type of gas?
options: Average KE per molecule at same T
Cᵥ per mole at same T
Mean free path at same T,P
explain: Average KE per molecule = (3/2)kT depends only on T, same for all ideal gases.

subject: Physics
prompt: In kinetic theory, gas pressure arises due to?
explain: Pressure results from rate of momentum transfer by molecules colliding with container walls.

subject: Physics
prompt: Number of vibrational modes for a nonlinear triatomic molecule?
explain: 3N−6 = 3(3)−6 = 3 vibrational modes for nonlinear triatomic (N=3).

subject: Physics
prompt: Number of vibrational modes for a linear triatomic molecule?
explain: 3N−5 = 3(3)−5 = 4 vibrational modes for linear triatomic (N=3).

subject: Physics
prompt: At same T and P, which property is equal for all ideal gas samples of same volume?
explain: Avogadro's law: equal volumes at same T and P contain equal number of molecules.

subject: Physics
prompt: Partial pressure of a gas in mixture = ?
explain: Each component contributes partial pressure Pᵢ = nᵢkT/V independently (Dalton's law).

subject: Physics
prompt: The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution is a plot of?
explain: Maxwell speed distribution plots number of molecules per unit speed interval (dN/dv) vs speed v.

subject: Physics
prompt: At constant T, fraction of molecules with speed > vₘₚ is approximately?
explain: Maxwell distribution is right-skewed; more than half the molecules have speed above vₘₚ.

subject: Physics
prompt: For an ideal gas, PV = NkT where N is?
explain: N is the total number of molecules; k is Boltzmann constant; compare with PV = nRT.

subject: Physics
prompt: Collision frequency Z at constant V is proportional to T as?
explain: Z = √2·π·d²·n·v̄; at const V, n is fixed and v̄ ∝ √T, so Z ∝ √T.

subject: Physics
prompt: Mean free path λ is independent of which quantity (at fixed T)?
explain: λ = 1/(√2·π·d²·n); it depends on n and d, but not on molecular mass.

subject: Physics
prompt: At constant T, if volume of ideal gas is halved, mean free path λ?
explain: Halving V doubles n (number density); λ = 1/(√2·π·d²·n), so λ halves.

subject: Physics
prompt: For ideal gas, PV/T = constant is valid for?
explain: PV/T = nR = constant only when number of moles n is fixed.

subject: Physics
prompt: Pressure of ideal gas: if T constant and V halved, collision frequency with wall?
explain: Halving V doubles n (number density), doubling collision rate → pressure doubles.

subject: Physics
prompt: Average translational KE of gas is directly proportional to?
explain: Translational KE = (3/2)kT; linear in absolute temperature T.

subject: Physics
prompt: In kinetic theory, temperature is a measure of?
explain: Temperature is a measure of average translational KE of molecules: (3/2)kT.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which gas effuses fastest at same T and P: He, Ne, Ar, Kr?
explain: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M; He has smallest M → fastest effusion.

subject: Physics
prompt: Internal energy U of n moles of triatomic nonlinear gas at T (f=6)?
explain: f=6 for nonlinear triatomic; U = (f/2)nRT = 3nRT.

subject: Physics
prompt: At constant volume, Cᵥ is related to internal energy U as?
explain: Cᵥ = (1/n)(∂U/∂T)_V ; fundamental definition of molar heat capacity at constant volume.

subject: Physics
prompt: Total number of vibrational degrees of freedom for CO₂ (linear, 3 atoms)?
explain: Linear molecule: vibrational modes = 3N−5 = 3(3)−5 = 4 modes.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which quantity determines whether a gas behaves ideally?
explain: At high T and low P, intermolecular forces and volume effects are negligible → ideal behavior.

subject: Physics
prompt: In Maxwell speed distribution, area under the curve represents?
explain: The total area under the Maxwell distribution curve equals the total number of molecules N.

subject: Physics
prompt: At same T, ratio of rms speed of N₂ (M=28) to CO (M=28) is?
explain: vᵣₘₛ depends only on M; N₂ and CO have same M=28 → same rms speed.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of these changes the mean free path of gas molecules?
explain: λ = 1/(√2πd²n); depends on molecular diameter d and number density n.

subject: Physics
prompt: Ratio of rms speed of gas to its most probable speed vₘₚ is?
explain: vᵣₘₛ = √(3RT/M), vₘₚ = √(2RT/M); ratio = √(3/2).

subject: Physics
prompt: The product nkT gives which quantity for an ideal gas?
explain: P = nkT where n is number density; this is the ideal gas law per unit volume.

subject: Physics
prompt: Translational KE to total KE ratio for monatomic gas (f=3) is?
explain: Monatomic gas has only translational DOF (f=3); all KE is translational → ratio = 1.

subject: Physics
prompt: Translational KE to total KE ratio for rigid diatomic gas (f=5) is?
explain: 3 translational DOF out of 5 total → ratio = 3/5.

subject: Physics
prompt: At same T, which has greater internal energy: 1 mol He or 1 mol O₂?
explain: O₂ (f=5): U=(5/2)RT > He (f=3): U=(3/2)RT at same T.

subject: Physics
prompt: For an ideal gas, work done in free expansion (vacuum) is?
explain: Free expansion: P_external = 0, so W = P_ext·ΔV = 0; also ΔU = 0 for ideal gas.

subject: Physics
prompt: In kinetic theory, the pressure on wall arises from change in _____ of molecules.
explain: Molecules bounce off wall; rate of change of linear momentum per unit area = pressure.
